title: App Service Health Metrics

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.33 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.33 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:metrics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" resourceType="Microsoft.Web/sites" (metric_name="HttpQueueLength" OR metric_name="AverageResponseTime" OR metric_name="HealthCheckStatus")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.33_app_service_health_metri_33"
| sort -_time
description: HTTP queue length, response time, and instance health explain user-visible slowness before 5xx rates spike.
value: Detecting app service health metrics early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Stream App Service metrics via diagnostic settings. Correlate with App Service Plan saturation (UC-4.2.28). Alert on sustained queue depth or failed health probes. Scale out or warm up instances.
visualization: Line chart (queue, response time, health), Table (app, metric, value), Status grid (probe per slot).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:metrics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Stream App Service metrics via diagnostic settings. Correlate with App Service Plan saturation (UC-4.2.28). Alert on sustained queue depth or failed health probes. Scale out or warm up instances.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" resourceType="Microsoft.Web/sites" (metric_name="HttpQueueLength" OR metric_name="AverageResponseTime" OR metric_name="HealthCheckStatus")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.33_app_service_health_metri_33"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:metrics` in `index=azure` to detect app service health metrics. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_33_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (queue, response time, health), Table (app, metric, value), Status grid (probe per slot)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of app service health metrics so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
